transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?
I came in because I feel wound up almost all day. It’s like my body is bracing for something, even when I’m just sitting at my computer or trying to relax after dinner.
How long have you been experiencing this feeling of being wound up?
About thirteen months now. It started around when my sister in Arecibo began needing a lot more help from the family.
Aside from your sister's situation, do you find yourself worrying excessively about other everyday matters or areas of your life?

Yes. My mind jumps from one thing to the next—my sister, whether I forgot something at work, my husband driving home, church commitments, bills. I keep preparing for problems that haven’t even happened.
Do you find it difficult to control or stop these worries once they start?

Yes, it’s hard to stop. I’ll tell myself, “Daniela, enough—just focus on this report,” but then one little thought turns into several more. Before I know it, I’ve spent half an hour checking messages or going over everything that could go wrong.
Do you have any diagnosed medical conditions or physical health problems?
No, I don’t have any diagnosed medical conditions that I know of.
Have you been having trouble falling or staying asleep?

Most nights I fall asleep eventually, but I wake up around three or four in the morning thinking about my sister’s next appointment or a server issue at work. Even if I get enough hours, I wake up feeling like I didn’t really rest.
